newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch shares dropped sharply on Monday as a sliding dollar and domestic bond market sapped investor confidence and sent buyers scurrying for cover.
The AEX index of 25 blue chip stocks closed 12.66 points, 1.65 percent, easier at 753.40, near the day's low at 750.57.
Dealers noted that the fall had not attracted much volume and said the lack of buyers was the pricipal factor more than any aggressive selling of short positions.
"The lack of interest was on the buying side today just as it was on the selling side on Friday," one said, referring to the market's Wall Street-inspired eight point jump on Friday.
"It was a story about the dollar and bond markets today -- no real equity news," added another.
There were no majors reporting earnings figures today but niche computer player Tulip posted a ten million guilder loss for 1996 against a similar-size profit a year earlier.
The shares ended 0.40 guilders down at 14.00, despite the company saying it expected to return to profit in 1997.

Cable maker Twentsche Kabel also announced net profits for 1996. It posted a net at 54.3 million guilders against 47.6 million in 1995. The shares were spared the sharp losses seen elsewhere, ending 0.10 off at 86.80 guilders.

Financial stocks, which are sensetive to movements in the index as a whole, were among those with the heaviest losses. Banking group ING slipped 2.20 guilders to 76.10 and ABN AMRO was 3.60 easier at 133.20 guilders.
Dutch chartists said the AEX was beginning to show some short-term wobbles but a break out of the current trading range either way has yet to be confirmed.
"We state that staying Neutral...is the best strategy on the short-term. For the scenarios on either side we advise to maintain close and trailing exit stops," ABN AMRO said.
